## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Sort in_review items in the Herdr selection list (WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

The `In Review` section of the Herdr selection list is ordered only by priority today, so producers and agents must scan the entire review queue to find actionable items; the desired behaviour is a deterministic sub-sort within the `In Review` group that surfaces the most urgent items first, using audit and flag state: `needsProducerReview=true` → fresh failed audit → stale failed audit → no audit → stale passed audit → remaining fresh passed audits.

## Users

- **Producers reviewing the queue** — scan the `In Review` section to decide what to review/close next.
  - *Story:* As a producer, I want failed audits (fresh first, then stale) at the top of `In Review` so the most problematic items are not buried behind un-audited or passed items.
- **Agents/dispatcher selecting review work** — pick the most urgent in_review item to act on.
  - *Story:* As an agent browsing the Herdr list, I want `needsProducerReview` items first, then failed audits, so producer-blocked work is surfaced first and the dispatcher consumes the correct head.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — In-Review bucket order (6 buckets):** Within the single last-positioned `In Review` group (`stage=in_review` items after regrouping), items are rendered in exactly this producer-confirmed bucket order: (1) `needsProducerReview=true` (any audit state), (2) fresh `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)==true`), (3) stale `auditResult=false` (`readyToClose=false` with `isAuditFresh==false` and `auditedAt` present), (4) no audit (`auditResult==null` or `auditedAt==null`), (5) stale `auditResult=true` (`readyToClose=true` with `isAuditFresh==false`), (6) remaining fresh `auditResult=true`. Within each bucket, items are sorted by priority `high → medium → low`, then by `id` as a deterministic tie-break.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mirrored ordering (Herdr + CLI + list):** The same bucket order applies in all `In Review` renderings: the Herdr regrouped worklist (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` `regroupWorkItems`), `wl next --groups` (`src/commands/grouping.ts`), and `wl list` stage-filtered In Review queries (`wl list --stage in_review` via `src/commands/list.ts` / shared list ordering). Any view that renders the `In Review` section uses the identical bucket predicate.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cross-group regression:** Non-`in_review` groups (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`) keep their existing group order and within-group sort (`in_progress → plan_complete → intake_complete → remaining`, then priority). Exactly one `In Review` section still renders, positioned last, with no duplicate headings.
- [ ] **AC4 — Freshness uses `isAuditFresh`:** `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, 60 s buffer) is the sole freshness predicate; flag-only flips of `needsProducerReview` do not make an audit stale (per WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R), and `auditedAt == updatedAt` atomics keep an immediately-audited item fresh. Stale buckets require `auditedAt` present; absence is the "no audit" bucket, not stale.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests & docs:** Unit tests cover every bucket (fresh-failed, stale-failed, no audit, stale-passed, fresh-passed, plus `needsProducerReview` precedence) with priority and `id` tie-break within a bucket, plus regroup/list integration tests that the merged Herdr list, `wl next`, and `wl list --stage in_review` all honour the bucket order; grouping comments/README note the 6-bucket order and reference this work item.
- [ ] **AC6 — Duplicate coverage:** `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` requirements are fully subsumed by this item's ACs; close `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` as a duplicate of this item.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new ordering, including `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`, and list/next command tests.

> Standard criteria also apply:
> - All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
> - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep bucket logic pure and dependency-free inside the sort path (same duplication rationale as `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Herdr has zero npm deps; a mirrored implementation is required in `src/commands/grouping.ts`/`list.ts`/`next.ts` so Herdr and CLI render identically).
- Reuse `isAuditFresh` from `@worklog/shared/icons` — do not re-implement freshness.
- Do not change how `In Review` membership is decided (still `stage=in_review` regardless of `status`/`priority`); this item only reorders inside the group.

## Existing state

- Herdr `In Review` today holds all `stage=in_review` items (critical-excluded) as a single group rendered last, sorted by `compareGroupableItems` (stage tie → priority → `id`); no audit/flag bucketing.
- `WorkItem` carries `needsProducerReview?: boolean`, `auditResult?: boolean|null`, `auditedAt?: string|null`, `updatedAt?: string`; `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` and `src/commands/helpers.ts`/`grouping.ts`) populates them and `isAuditFresh` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) defines staleness (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`).
- `assignItemGroups`/`regroupWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) and `src/commands/grouping.ts` implement group order `Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review`; `selectWorkItems`/`fetchNextItems` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) compose the final displayed list preserved by regrouping.
- `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` ("Sort in_review items in the section list by audit status", `open`, `medium`, `sortIndex 7300`) described a compatible but incomplete bucket phrasing (`needsProducerReview → missing audit → stale → passed`) that omitted the fresh/stale-failed distinction; per producer confirmation it is a duplicate of this item and should be closed.
- `wl list --stage in_review` today returns `isAuditFresh`-agnostic order; `wl next --groups` groups `In Review` but does not bucket-sort it.
- Related past fixes: `WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW` (duplicate In Review sections + group order), `WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW` (in_review stage filter), `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` (atomic `auditedAt=updatedAt`).

## Desired change

- Extend the `In Review` rendering order so that after the canonical group assignment, items inside group `In Review` are stable-sorted by the 6-bucket order `(needsProducerReview → fresh-failed → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → fresh-passed)` with secondary `priority` + `id` ordering. Apply it in: (a) the Herdr regroup path (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` `regroupWorkItems` / new `compareInReviewItems` helper used for the In Review slice), (b) the CLI grouping path (`src/commands/grouping.ts` + `src/commands/next.ts` grouping emission), and (c) the CLI list path (`src/commands/list.ts` or the shared list sort) so `wl list --stage in_review` renders the same order. Keep the overall contracts (no filtering, deterministic ordering, mandatory items preserved) and ensure Herdr and CLI agree.
- Close `WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV` as a duplicate once coverage is verified.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `regroupWorkItems` extension + new `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` helper for the 6-bucket order; primary fix location.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — bucket-order tests for all 6 buckets, priority/`id` tie-break, plus regroup integration test.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — mirrored `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` for CLI grouping so `wl next --groups` matches Herdr.
- `src/commands/list.ts` (+ shared list-sort helper if used) — apply same bucket order for `wl list --stage in_review` (and any filtered list rendering In Review).
- `src/commands/next.ts` — ensure grouped `In Review` emission honours the bucket order.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — mirrored CLI bucket-order tests.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` freshness predicate (reference; atomic updatedAt=auditedAt behaviour).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem` `needsProducerReview`/`auditResult`/`auditedAt` population via `normalizeItem` (reference; field availability).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — extend if In Review rendering order is asserted there.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` and grouping code comments — document the 6-bucket In Review order.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV** — "Sort in_review items in the section list by audit status" (`open`, `medium`) — duplicate intent confirmed by producer; to be closed as `duplicate` of this item (this brief subsumes its requirements; its `needsProducerReview → missing → stale → passed` phrasing is a shorthand for the full 6-bucket order defined here).
- **WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW** — "Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order)" (`completed`, `medium`) — established the single last-positioned `In Review` section and Critical/Group N file-path grouping preserved here.
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW** — "Herdr: in_review stage filter (f-r) shows 0 items because stage-filtered fetch restricts to status=open" (`completed`, `high`) — established that `in_review` items carry `completed`/`in-progress` status and must be fetched specially.
- **WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 / WL-0MTHRW3770014H51** — atomic `saveAuditResult: updatedAt=auditedAt` and `isAuditFresh` 60 s window; governs the fresh vs stale distinction used by buckets 2/3/5/6.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** — "Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head" (`in-progress`, `critical`) — dispatcher that will consume the newly-ordered head; consuming the sorted In Review order is the downstream value.
- **WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z** — narrow-pane header truncation (`in_review`, `high`, `needsProducerReview:true`) — unrelated rendering concern, noted only to avoid chrome-budget interaction.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale vs fresh failed precedence:** Producer confirmed that fresh failed (`readyToClose=false` + fresh) outranks stale failed, and stale failed outranks `no audit`; stale passed outranks only the fresh-passed rest. Assumption: within each bucket, priority `high→medium→low` then `id` is the tie-break (from WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV's "within each group sort by priority").
- **Scope-creep risk:** Stage/priority changes inside `In Review`, new `In Review` splitting across multiple headings, or changing membership (e.g. filtering by `needsProducerReview`) are out of scope; record as linked follow-ups, not in-scope.
- **Duplication maintenance:** CLI grouping and Herdr grouping must mirror the same bucket helper to avoid divergence (same rationale as Q2c duplication); keep the logic pure and tested in both places.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is the exact bucket order inside `In Review`? The description lists needsProducerReview=true first, then audit with readyToClose=false, then no audit, then stale audit, then the rest — but related WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV phrases it as needsProducerReview=true, followed by audit missing, followed by audit stale then audit passed (no mention of the readyToClose=false bucket). Please confirm the canonical 5-bucket order and whether stale-failed and stale-passed both belong in the stale bucket or if failed audits should always outrank stale audits." — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "needsProducerReview=true → audit readyToClose=false → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → rest". Interpretation applied: 6 buckets = `needsProducerReview` → fresh `readyToClose=false` → stale `readyToClose=false` → no audit → stale `readyToClose=true` → fresh `readyToClose=true` (within each bucket: high→medium→low→id). The first `readyToClose=false` bucket is fresh-failed; the explicit `stale-failed` bucket is stale-failed; stale-passed is stale-passed. Source: interactive reply. Research: inspected `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:279` (`isAuditFresh`), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (In Review single-last group), `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (WorkItem fields), `src/commands/grouping.ts` (CLI grouping).
- Q: "Should `needsProducerReview` be a bucket for the whole In Review group or a flag that just bubbles flagged items to the very front regardless of audit status?" — Answer (producer, implied by bucket list): it is the topmost bucket covering the whole group — any `needsProducerReview=true` item precedes every non-flagged In Review item regardless of audit state.
- Q: "Does the bucket order apply only to the Herdr plugin or also to `wl next --groups` / CLI In Review rendering?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "wl next mirrors" — CLI grouping mirrors the Herdr bucket order so both render identically.
- Q: "Should `wl list --stage in_review` and the `--priority`/`--status` filtered lists also apply the same In Review bucket order, or only the default/browse worklist?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "wl list shows same ordering" — the same 6-bucket order applies to `wl list` In Review renderings.
- Q: "WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV describes a near-duplicate sort for in_review items. Should it be closed as a duplicate of this item after intake, or kept as a separate follow-up?" — Answer (producer 2026-09-04): "close as duplicate (check this item covers all requirements)" — WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV closes as duplicate of this item; this brief explicitly subsumes its requirements (see AC6 and Related work).
- Additional related docs inspected: `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `src/commands/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/list.ts`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `wl show WL-0MTC0WT3Y008O4LV --json`.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Extend `regroupWorkItems` with `inReviewBucket`/`compareInReviewItems` for the 6-bucket Herdr In Review order (`needsProducerReview → fresh-failed → stale-failed → no audit → stale-passed → fresh-passed`, priority/`id` tie-break).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — Add 6-bucket and priority tie-break tests + merged-list In Review bucket integration test.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` + `src/commands/next.ts` — Mirror the same bucket helper for `wl next --groups` CLI In Review grouping.
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Apply the same bucket order for `wl list --stage in_review` filtered In Review rendering.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` freshness predicate (reference; atomic updatedAt=auditedAt).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem` `needsProducerReview`/`auditResult`/`auditedAt` population via `normalizeItem`.

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.

## Problem statement

Two coupled defects leave valid audits visible as stale ("out of date audit"):

1. **Comment bumps invalidate audits.** `wl comment add` -> `createComment` -> `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (packages/shared/src/database.ts:3282, persistent-store `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` ~3416) advances the work item `updatedAt` for ANY comment. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (packages/shared/src/icons.ts:269) compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`; a comment added after the audit (e.g. "Audit re-evaluation (forced --force)" on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B at 21:26:17Z vs audit 21:21:03Z) therefore flips the audit to stale even though no content changed. The documented guarantee in icons.ts ("Flag-only flips of needsProducerReview do not move updatedAt, so a previously valid audit remains fresh") does NOT cover comments - comments are the common case that breaks it.

2. **Audit persistence does not atomically update auditedAt.** `wl audit-set` (src/commands/audit-result.ts) writes the `audit_results` row (auditedAt = now) but does not touch the work item; `wl update --audit-text` (src/commands/update.ts) also only writes `saveAuditResult`. There is no single atomic operation that both records the audit AND refreshes the freshness clock, so a comment between audit and display (or a re-evaluation that comments instead of persisting - see WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF) leaves the record behind `updatedAt`.

Investigation outcome - audit-content comments can be removed (no consumer parses them):
- implement skill: reads the audit **record** (`/skill:audit` -> runner -> `wl audit-show`; `audit_report_<id>.md`); comments are only generic context in Step 4 ("pay attention to comments"), never parsed as verdicts
- ship skill `check-audit-gate.js`: `wl audit-show` -> `readyToClose`/`rawOutput`/`summary`; `wl comment add` is used only to WRITE merge logs
- heartbeat, report skill, herdr TUI (`worklist.ts`, icons): all read `auditResult`/`auditedAt` from the record

So the audit verdict must live in the audit record only; audits duplicated in comments are dead weight and actively harmful (they bump updatedAt).

Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

1. **Freshness clock:** make audit freshness reflect content-only changes. Options to evaluate (pick one, document trade-offs):
   a. exclude comments (and `needsProducerReview` flag flips, already excluded) from `updatedAt` bumps via `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`; or
   b. `isAuditFresh` uses a content/activity fingerprint rather than `updatedAt`; or
   c. `wl audit-set`/`--audit-text` perform an atomic "record audit + set updatedAt = auditedAt" so a later comment still breaks it (not fully fixing) - likely insufficient alone.
2. **Atomic audit persistence:** `wl audit-set` (and/or `wl update --audit-text`) should be a single operation that records the `audit_results` row and refreshes the item's freshness marker so "audit recorded" always implies "audit fresh" immediately.
3. **Remove audit-content comments:** stop adding the audit report/verdict to work-item comments (the verdict lives in the audit record). Keep comments for dispatches/trails (herdr "Auto-dispatched..." is a dispatch marker, not audit content - out of scope) and for human annotations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a post-audit comment is added, the audit remains fresh: `wl show <id> --json` + a comment -> `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` stays true; TUI keeps the passed icon, not stale (add a regression test in packages/shared tests for the chosen mechanism)
- [ ] `wl audit-set` is atomic: after it, `auditedAt >= updatedAt` immediately (no intermediate window where a read shows stale) - or the alternative chosen mechanism guarantees the same
- [ ] The audit report/verdict is no longer duplicated into work-item comments by audit flows; existing duplicated comments on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B are documented as legacy (no migration required unless trivially safe)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: comment-after-audit keeps fresh; audit-then-comment ordering matches the chosen freshness clock; `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically to `wl audit-set`
- [ ] Docs updated: icons.ts guarantee comment, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md (or equivalent), audit SKILL.md where it describes the audit record as canonical

Chosen approach: `wl audit-set` atomically sets `updatedAt = auditedAt`.

# Single machine-wide downtime leader across all worklogs (replace per-worklog elections) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Downtime leadership is **per-worklog** (`coordinationDir: join(targetCwd, '.worklog')`): every open project tab runs its own election, lease/lock, and `downtime-coordination.json`. The refactor WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Multi-worklog support describe a leader that "compares offers across directories" — but no instance ever sees another worklog's offers, so that behaviour does not exist. Result: N independent leaders poll the same shared llama-proxy, oversubscribe its slot budget, and each provide only ~1 item/hour throughput while zombie leases compound divergence.

## Users

- **Herdr users with multiple project tabs open** — want a single machine-wide downtime dispatch queue so idle LLM capacity is shared fairly and not oversubscribed when two projects are idle simultaneously.
  - *Story:* As a user with TCE + ContextHub tabs open, I want the downtime leader to dispatch the globally highest-priority offer (e.g. ContextHub audit before TCE intake) and respect a single slot budget, so two projects never launch 2-slot audits at once.
- **Operators observing downtime logs** — want one coordination file, one lease, one dispatch log to inspect, instead of per-worklog fragments.
- **Agents dispatched via downtime** — benefit from higher global throughput (no per-project 1h cooldown starvation) and correct cross-project tier ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — One shared coordination dir:** A second herdr instance opened on a *different* worklog joins the same coordination file; the file contains entries with different `worklogRoot`s.
- [ ] **AC2 — Exactly one leader machine-wide:** With N instances across P worklogs, only one holds a valid lease and no two instances dispatch in the same tick window (tested for the zombie case WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD).
- [ ] **AC3 — Cross-directory tier dispatch:** Leader orders offers by existing tier priority (audit → critical-first → implement → plan → intake) *across* worklog roots and spawns the pane in the entry's `worklogRoot`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Global slot budget:** With 3 proxy slots and 2 projects offering work, total concurrently dispatched/requesting work never exceeds the shared budget (no cross-project oversubscription).
- [ ] **AC5 — Safe migration:** Existing per-worklog coordination files stop being written once the machine dir is authoritative; no double-dispatch during transition; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` updated to match actual behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & build green:** Headless tests prove AC1–AC4 invariants; full herdr test suite + `npm run build` green.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section, and code comments reflect the machine-wide design; CHANGELOG excluded (ship skill owns it).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- Must land after WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (cooldown stall) and WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (zombie lease) — both now `completed` (blocked-by satisfied).
- Coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches) on the machine slot budget — single budget, not per-project.
- Single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) out of scope.
- File-lock + lease model reused from `leader-election.ts`; machine dir default `~/.herdr/downtime/` with `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` env override.
- Fail-safe: unreadable/missing coordination or lease files degrade to "no dispatch this cycle", never crash or drop another instance's entry.
- Must not double-dispatch during migration (a TCE instance with an old TCE file must not ALSO join the machine file with different `instanceId`).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` reads/writes `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` with per-instance `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` manages file lock + 5-min lease per worklog.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `createDowntimeWorker` wires `coordinationDir: join(targetCwd, '.worklog')` — the per-worklog coupling to replace.

- Related fixes landed: zombie lease fix, cooldown probe-before-pause, per-tick re-derivation.

## Desired change

- Introduce **machine-scoped coordination dir** (default `~/.herdr/downtime/`, env override `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`) containing `coordination.json`, `leader-lease.json`, `leader.lock`, `dispatches.log` (or equivalent names).
- All instances read/write the **same** coordination + lease/lock files regardless of project; each entry carries `worklogRoot` (today's `directory` field, renamed or retained).
- **One election, one lease** machine-wide (reuse `leader-election.ts` against the machine dir); lease survives no-candidate cooldowns (depends on zombie fix — done).
- **Leader dispatches across directories** by tier priority, spawning panes into each entry's `worklogRoot` (viaroot `wl` invocation as today); stale-entry pruning and 30-min check-in cadence carry over per instance.
- **Machine slot budget** enforced by the leader against shared proxy status (coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q).
- **Migration/fallback:** prefer machine dir when authoritative; retire legacy `.worklog/downtime-*` files; document retirement; no double-join.
- Correct `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (and package README) to describe actual behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — Switch coordination file/dir resolution to machine-scoped dir; `worklogRoot` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — Point lock/lease at machine dir.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Wire machine dir into `createDowntimeWorker` / `runCoordinationCheckIn` / `dispatchFromCoordination`; migration logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Rolling logs under machine dir or per-worklog (decide).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Pass machine coordination dir into worker wiring.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Correct multi-worklog section, file paths, env override.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update downtime worker overview if it mentions file paths.
- `packages/herdr/tests/*.test.ts` (+ new headless tests for AC1–AC4) — Machine-wide invariants.

## Related work

- **Depends on (completed):** WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (empty-file cooldown stall), WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (zombie lease) — both `completed`.
- **Coordinate with:** WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches, `in_progress`) — machine slot budget is the shared concern.

- **Downtime family:** WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (spare-capacity dispatch), WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL etc. — prior cadence/budget context.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Migration double-dispatch:** Mitigation — single machine dir authoritative; legacy files not written once migrated; instanceId stays stable across dirs; test with mixed old/new files.
- **File-lock contention on shared dir:** Mitigation — reuse existing `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` + lease pattern; no new concurrency primitive.
- **Worklog root path stability:** Assumption — `directory`/`worklogRoot` is the worklog root (parent of `.worklog`), not cwd; spawn uses `worklogRoot` for `wl` invocation.
- **Scope creep — multi-machine, audit parallelism, new tier kinds:** Record as separate work items, not in scope.
- **Env override discoverability:** Document `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` in docs and settings/README.

## Open Questions

- None blocking intake — design details (exact file names in machine dir, dispatch log location, migration flag) to be settled in plan.

## Problem

The `wl sync` command uses a binary author-identity gate: it either allows ALL commits from the configured user.email or rejects them all. When syncing against a remote with commits from a different author identity (e.g., a different email address), sync fails with a hard error.

This is annoying for single-operator repos with multiple machines/emails (false positives) and does not scale for team or CI scenarios.

## Proposed Solution

Replace the binary allow/deny gate with a configurable **author whitelist** (`syncAllowedAuthors`) in `.worklog/worklog.yaml`:

- **Empty list (default)** - same behavior as now: only accept commits from the local user.email (strictest, no change to current security posture)
- **Non-empty list** - accept commits from any email in the whitelist
- **null or true** - allow any author (current --allow-foreign-author behavior)

### Example config

Empty list (default / most secure):
  syncAllowedAuthors: []

Allow specific additional authors:
  syncAllowedAuthors:
    - sorra@thewizardscode.com
    - alice@company.com

Allow all (explicit opt-in):
  syncAllowedAuthors: null

### Implementation points

1. Add syncAllowedAuthors to worklog config schema (in config.defaults.yaml and validation)
2. Modify the sync author-check logic to read syncAllowedAuthors from config, check commit author email against the list
3. Update --allow-foreign-author CLI flag to set/override the config value
4. Update help text and docs to explain the whitelist model
5. Add tests covering: empty list, non-empty list, null/true, mismatch

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New syncAllowedAuthors config key accepted and validated
- [ ] Default empty list enforces current behavior (only local author)
- [ ] Non-empty whitelist allows commits from listed emails
- [ ] Null/true allows all authors (equivalent to current --allow-foreign-author)
- [ ] --allow-foreign-author flag still works (sets config to null or true)
- [ ] Tests: empty list, non-empty list, null/true, author mismatch rejection
- [ ] Help text explains the whitelist model
- [ ] Existing --allow-foreign-author users are unaffected

## Goal

## Problem

`wl comment add` calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` which updates `updatedAt`.
The `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` check in icons.ts returns false when

Option (c) - atomic audit persistence: `wl audit-set` (and `wl update --audit-text`)

recording an audit. This ensures that immediately after an audit, the freshness
check always passes, regardless of subsequent comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl audit-set` sets updatedAt = auditedAt (or later) atomically with the audit record
- [ ] `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically
- [ ] After audit, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true immediately
- [ ] No race window where a read between audit-set and display sees stale data

## Goal

Stop audit flows from duplicating audit results into work-item comments.

## Problem

The `audit_pr.py` `append_audit_comment()` function writes the full audit
result as a comment on the work item. This is redundant because:

- The audit verdict lives in the audit record (audit_results table)
- The implement skill reads the audit record, not comments
- The ship skill reads the audit record
- The heartbeat and TUI read the audit record

The comment is actively harmful: it calls `wl comment add` which bumps

## Problem
Between 01:00–now 2026-09-02 the TCE per-worklog `downtime-dispatches.log` showed 5 aggregate pauses:

`"Downtime worker: 3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms."`

Only the 3-strike aggregate is written via `deps.recordError()` -> `appendDowntimeLogEntry()` (`index.ts:998`/`downtime-log.ts:268`), with no stderr/exitCode/timeoutMs/workItemId/probe context.

Machine-wide dispatch is now authoritative (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` + `downtime-leader-lease.json`), but logs stay per-worklog (`downtime-log.ts:5` F6 WL-0MTII4CWT00452HU + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md:222`) for per-project observability — aggregate + per-strike logs must be queryable.

## Problem
Operators investigating overnight dispatches must know the machine-wide vs per-worklog log architecture, then aggregate `*/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` across projects themselves. There is no single command to produce a 24h dispatch report.

A `dispatch-logs` skill in the ContextHub project (`.pi/skills/dispatch-logs/`) that, when invoked via `/skill:dispatch-logs` (or `skill:dispatch-logs --hours 6 --since 2026-09-01T20:00:00Z --project ContextHub`), produces a concise human-readable report of all dispatch activity.

### Default behaviour
- Window: last 24 hours from `Date.now()`.
- Search all worklog roots for files matching `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Parse each file for lines matching `Downtime worker:` or `Dispatch completed` or `ERROR` or `DOWNTIME`.
- Also read `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` and `downtime-leader-lease.json` for leader identity and active dispatch target.
- Produce a report with:
  1. **Leader summary** — leader ID, acquired-at, active project, leader lock file.
  2. **Dispatch timeline** — chronological list of all dispatches with timestamp, project root, dispatch type (audit/implement/plan/intake), work-item ID, and status.
  3. **Error summary** — consecutive-wl-error pauses, timestamps, duration, and project.
  4. **Coordination state** — current coordination file contents (leader, active project, last dispatch).
  5. **Known issues** — if per-strike detail is missing, note that per-strike stderr/exitCode are not available yet (tracked by companion debug item).

### Invocation
```
/skill:dispatch-logs                  # default: last 24h, all projects
/skill:dispatch-logs --hours 6        # last 6 hours
/skill:dispatch-logs --since 2026-09-01T20:00:00Z --until 2026-09-02T02:00:00Z  # custom window
```

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher consistently selects and dispatches work items that do not appear in the herdr extensions selection list, so two first-class "next most important item" selectors disagree. - "As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been visible in the herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen."
- "As a maintainer, I want a documented ranking contract so I can tell whether a divergence is a bug or an intentional tier policy."

1. **Divergence diagnosed with evidence** — the brief/records cite the exact code paths compared (herdr `fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` + `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` + `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` vs downtime `downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` + `src/commands/next.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts:filterCandidates/findNextWorkItemFromItems/computeScore/reSort`) and a reproducible sample where the two selectors disagree (e.g. `wl next -n N` output vs herdr rendered list vs downtime tier chosen).

# Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier

## Problem statement

The scheduled-prompts tier (WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX; `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`) only supports best-effort frequency in whole days (`intervalDays` via `isDueScheduledPrompt`: due iff `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays`). There is no way to pin a prompt to a time of day, so a daily standup cannot be made to run at a specific wall-clock time (e.g. 06:05) and instead fires whenever the next idle slot appears after the interval elapses — too early/late for a daily standup window.

## Users

- Operators who want a prompt (notably the daily standup, `/skill:standup`) to run at a specific time of day, not just once per N days whenever an idle slot appears.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to add an optional `time` field (e.g. `06:05`) to a scheduled-prompt entry so the system dispatches it in the first available idle window **after** that time, so the standup runs at 06:05 each day.
- As an operator, when `time` is absent the existing behaviour is unchanged (due iff `now - last >= intervalDays`), so existing entries like `/skill:refactor` keep working without config changes.
- As an operator, I want `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` and provisioned `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` to set `/skill:standup` to 06:05, so a fresh worklog gets the correct daily standup time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add optional `time?: string` to `ScheduledPrompt` (`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`). When absent, behaviour is identical to today (backward-compatible). Valid values are wall-clock `HH:MM` 24-hour times (e.g. `06:05`); entries with an invalid `time` are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash), consistent with invalid `intervalDays`/prompt handling (AC7 of WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX).
2. Extend due-check semantics (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`): an entry with `time` is due only when BOTH (a) `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays * DAY_MS` (same interval gate as today) AND (b) `now` is at or after the `time` on the calendar day of `now` (local wall-clock). If `now` is before `time` today and the interval gate is otherwise satisfied, the entry is NOT due — it becomes due in the first idle window at/after `time`. A dispatched entry is NOT due again until the next calendar day's `time` has been reached and the interval has again elapsed (so a 06:05 daily entry dispatched at 07:00 today is not due again at 08:00 today).
3. `lastTriggeredAt` semantics ensure once-per-interval: after a timed dispatch, the interval comparison uses the actual dispatch time, so a missed `time` (e.g. no idle slot until 08:00) still counts as dispatched for that day and the next due time is tomorrow 06:05 (not 08:00 tomorrow and not immediately). Daily entries with `time` therefore fire at most once per calendar day.
4. Update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to include `/skill:standup` with `intervalDays: 1` and `time: "06:05"` (the canonical standup time). `src/commands/init.ts` provisioning remains create-if-absent; `wl init` on an existing repo must not clobber user edits — if the operator has customised scheduled prompts, re-running `wl init` leaves them untouched. New worklogs provisioned after this change get the timed standup entry.
5. Ensure `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` in the current checkout reflects `time: "06:05"` for `/skill:standup` (so the dev branch's live config matches the template).
6. Update documentation/comments to describe the `time` field (README / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` or equivalent downtime docs) and the "first window after time" semantics, including the backward-compat note when `time` is absent and the local wall-clock interpretation of `HH:MM`.
7. Unit/integration tests cover: parse of `time` (valid, absent, invalid → skipped), due-check with `time` (before-time not due, at/after-time due, interval gate interaction, once-per-day, missed-window becomes tomorrow), backward-compat (no `time` behaves as before), and the timed standup entry in the provisioned template.
8. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (no regressions).

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw (mirrors WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX constraints and `scheduled-prompts.ts` header).
- `time` is wall-clock local `HH:MM` (no timezone field, no cron); `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC ISO-8601 as today. The due check interprets `time` against local calendar day.
- Scheduled tier remains the first dispatch tier, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker; per-process single-flight guard still applies. No new timer infrastructure — reuse `createDowntimeWorker.tick`.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` (id/prompt/intervalDays/lastTriggeredAt), `parseScheduledPrompt`, `isDueScheduledPrompt`, `getDueScheduledPrompt`, `DAY_MS`; no `time` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` scheduled tier (freeze gate → scheduled → audit → …); `dispatchScheduledPrompt` with atomic `lastTriggeredAt` persist + rolling-log `scheduled` kind.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` + `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — base set is `/skill:refactor` (intervalDays 3) plus `/skill:standup` (intervalDays 1) with no `time`.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber).

## Desired change

Extend `ScheduledPrompt` with optional `time: "HH:MM"` and update the due-check to be "interval gate AND at-or-after time today" so timed entries dispatch in the first idle window after their wall-clock time. Set the canonical standup time to `06:05` in both the template and the live `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`. Update docs/tests accordingly. When `time` is absent, behaviour is identical to today.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add `time` field, validation, due-check extension.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — no structural change expected (consumes via `getDueScheduledPrompt`), but verify tier interaction / dispatch semantics for timed entries.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup`.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — add `time: "06:05"` to `/skill:standup` in the checkout so the dev branch reflects the template.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — no change expected beyond carrying the new template value (create-if-absent preserved).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` or `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — new/updated tests for `time` parse + due-check.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` / `CONFIG.md` / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header — document `time` field and "first window after time" semantics.

## Related work

- WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX — scheduled prompts tier (parent capability).
- Standup skill: `/skill:standup` + `generate_standup.py` (scheduled via this tier; canonical consumer of `06:05`).
- WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9 — provisioning / scheduled-prompts template.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `time` is `HH:MM` local wall-clock on the calendar day of `now`; seconds are not needed. `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC — the due check bridges them by comparing the local clock for `time` against `now` and the interval against `lastTriggeredAt`.
- Risk: "first window after time" depends on an idle slot appearing; if the machine is busy all day, the dispatch slips to the next idle window (still at most once per day due to `lastTriggeredAt` anchoring). This is the correct best-effort behaviour.
- Risk: DST / system clock skew — acceptable for best-effort `HH:MM` local semantics; clock-skew handling mirrors `isDueScheduledPrompt` today (future `lastTriggeredAt` → not due).
- Scope creep: cron expressions, timezone-aware schedules, per-entry model overrides — record separately, not this item.

But `runCoordinationCheckIn` re-offers only every `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS = 30min`. A non-leader's entry is offered at most once per 30min yet is pruned after 5min if no dispatch consumes it — 25min dead window where the leader sees no entry for that project.

Overnight this starved SorraAgents while ContextHub dispatched alone every ~30min (verified Sep 4: SorraAgents offered `SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z` at 06:39:39 -> dispatched 06:39:41 only when offer was fresh; earlier offers at 23:45,00:08,00:38 etc. were pruned before the next idle dispatch). The `critical first then round-robin (per-worklogRoot)` guarantee (`WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V` + =`WL-0MTJE0FXC006WAOX`) never got a chance — `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` only orders entries that are present.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — expects global `critical first, then round-robin across projects` as documented; overnight bias to one project erodes trust and delays other projects' ready work.
- **Herdr user with multiple project tabs open** — wants spare-capacity dispatch shared fairly, not oversubscribing one project's backlog.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl** — needs a single consistent contract for cross-project dispatch without TTL/check-in mismatch.

1. **Expiry removed** — `pruneStaleEntries` (and any equivalent TTL prune on `downtime-coordination.json`) is removed or disabled for the machine coordination file. No coordination entry is removed solely by wall-clock age. Legacy per-worklog files (if still read) follow the same rule.

The dispatcher itself can dispatch every `~70s` while idle (`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=10s` jittered ±50% + `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS=60s`, `worklist.ts:downtime` task not `paneGate.visible()`-gated, `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` idle gate). So even after WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P removes the `300s` `pruneStaleEntries` expiry (`dispatchFromCoordination:1638`, `DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS`), offers remain the bottleneck: with 4 projects, a burst of ~4 dispatches in ~4min when idle, then ~26min gap until next check-ins. Within one project, back-to-back items cannot dispatch continuously at the idle rate.

This follow-up to WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P shortens the offer cadence so the leader always has work to dispatch while idle, without reintroducing age-based expiry.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — expects spare-capacity dispatch to keep the machine busy while idle, not idle 26min of every 30min because offers are sparse.
- **Herdr user with multiple project tabs** — wants fair `critical first then round-robin` at the configured idle rate, not bursts gated by 30min check-ins.
- **Maintainer** — needs a single consistent contract: offers persist (WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P) and are refreshed fast enough to keep up with dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Check-in interval shortened** — `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS` reduced from `30min` to `5min` (or otherwise `<=5min`; integration test already uses `300_000` at `integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts:316`). Lower bound `>=60s` to avoid wl churn. `checkInIntervalMs` remains injectable via `DowntimeWorkerConfig` for tests.
2. **Post-dispatch re-offer** — when `dispatchFromCoordination` removes an entry (`removeEntry` on dispatched or claimed-but-failed spawn/marker), the owning instance re-offers its next `computeMostImportantItem` without waiting for the next interval (push-based). Minimal hook: leader notifies owner via coordination file observation, or owner watches its own entry removal on next `tick()` and immediately runs `runCoordinationCheckIn` (no extra poll when not idle). Fail-safe: file read failure still degrades to next interval.
3. **No expiry reintroduced** — `pruneStaleEntries` removal from WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P stays; this item does not reintroduce TTL pruning. Eligibility still validated at dispatch time (`fetchItem`+`classifyItemForDispatch`/`isAuditFresh` per WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P).
4. **Rate still gated by idle/slots** — dispatch still requires `evaluateIdle` + `perSlotTracker.thresholdMetCount` + `freeSlots >= DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS / DOWNTIME_PANE_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`; faster offers do not bypass idle or slot budgets. Probe semantics `WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7` (coordination empty = transient gap) unchanged.
5. **Tests & build green** — `downtime-worker`/`coordination-dispatch`/`integration-leader-dispatch` fixtures updated for new default interval and re-offer hook; `npm run build` + herdr suite green. Manual spot: overnight log shows >1 dispatch per 10min while idle with multiple projects offering.
6. **Docs updated** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section document new interval and re-offer behavior.

## Constraints

- Depends on WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P (expiry removal); do not reintroduce `pruneStaleEntries` for coordination entries.
- Do not touch ranking — `WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2` owns `dispatcher == Herdr list head`; reuse `computeMostImportantItem` pipeline.
- Fail-safe: unreadable coordination/lease files still degrade to no dispatch this cycle, never crash. No new npm deps.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:235` `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS = 30*60*1000`, `:2645` `checkInIntervalMs = opts.checkInIntervalMs ?? DEFAULT...`, `:2843` `lastCheckInAt` gate, `:1830` `runCoordinationCheckIn` (fail-open on `!ok`, removes entry on `noCandidate`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `downtime` scheduler task (poll `~10s` jittered, idle `60s`, not visibility-gated) → `createDowntimeWorker.tick()` → `dispatchFromCoordination` (tier `audit→critical(sortIndex)→implement→plan→intake`, `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` per `worklogRoot`).
- `WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P` removes `pruneStaleEntries(..., leaseTtlMs=300s)` (`:1638`, `DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS`) and adds dispatch-time `fetchItem` eligibility gate — leaves 30min offer sparsity.
- Tests: `integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts:316` uses `300_000` to stay inside old prune window; `coordination-dispatch.test.ts:667,784,834` assumes `30min` cadence.

## Desired change

1. Lower `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS` to `5min` (clamped `>=60s`).
2. Add immediate re-offer after dispatch: after `dispatchFromCoordination` removes the dispatched entry, the owner (on its next `tick()` or via a file-watch of its own `instanceId`) runs `runCoordinationCheckIn` out-of-band so the next idle window has a fresh offer.
